Remembering the B Turtle Bike Microcaravan: The Tiniest RV You Could Tow by e-Bike
33 photos
Photo: YouTube/Atik Family
The road to hell is paved with good intentions, broken dreams, failed startups, and amazing products that fail to catch on. Among them is the B Turtle, a bike microcaravan once in the running for the title of the world's smallest RV.
Technically, it wasn't an RV but a towable. B Turtle was an inflatable microcaravan designed to be towed by electric bike or even a pedal-powered one, if your legs were strong enough and up to the task. When not used for camping, it could be used as a plain bike cargo trailer, doubling up the functionality you got for the money.
The B Turtle, which you might also find spelled as B-Turtle, was launched in 2018 by Austrian tent specialist GentleTent and, for a few years afterwards, enjoyed great success. This was no starry-eyed startup promising the world and then discovering that "wanting" and "doing" were two, very different things; this was a company that launched a product and took it internationally, both to sell and to rent.
At one point, the B Turtle was available in Germany, its native Austria (of course), Sweden, the Netherlands, and even Ireland. You could either buy a unit or, if you were strapped for cash or still undecided, you could rent one to try out and see how it fared.
Photo: YouTube/Atik Family The first signs of trouble appeared when the e-bike bubble began losing air. By May 2024, GentleTent had gone through one bankruptcy filing and one restructuring, but not even that was enough to help it through the hard times. One year later, in May 2025, the company filed for bankruptcy for one last time and went into liquidation.
That means that the B Turtle, perhaps the neatest bike caravan ever created, slipped off the map. Production (obviously) shut down and all stock vanished, though you can probably still find a unit in good condition on the second market.
And that brings us to the video below: a rare, recent, real-life camping experience with the B Turtle, courtesy of content creators Atik Family. The Atik couple often try out the newest motorhomes and camping solutions, in partnership with select manufacturers and distributors, but this one is a true surprise.
Photo: GentleTent Somehow, they found a B Turtle and took it out on a windy overnight outing, getting to see for themselves what exactly made this product better than any other bikepacking product on the market.
For us, it's a great occasion to remember a bike microcaravan that had all the right ingredients, but one – affordability –, while we take a trip down memory lane.
The B Turtle was a heavy-duty bike cargo trailer with 12-inch wheels, a slide-out storage box and the tent structure on top, folded down and packed neatly in a weatherproof zipped back. In road mode, it looked just like a bike cargo trailer would: compact and relatively lightweight , so it would not pose too much of an issue hauling around.
Photo: GentleTent Exact dimensions for the B Turtle in travel mode were 113 x 73.5 x 79 cm (44.5 x 29 x 31 inches), with an empty weight of 29-kg (64-pound).
GentleTent said that setup at camp was a matter of 15 minutes, which included inflating the tent superstructure and anchoring all the parts to the ground for safety. As you can see in the Atiks' video, that number is relative to the weather and the terrain you plan on setting up camp. Obviously, setting up a tent in windy weather is not going to be that easy.
The B Turtle came with adjustable support legs, but you still had to anchor it like a traditional tent . Once that part was out of the way, inflating the upper part and the mattress was done by a 12V pump – now that was the easy part!
Photo: GentleTent The elevated platform held a two-person bed and it came with three zippered windows. In front, an awning-style section with an integrated floor created a lobby where you had full standing height, and that, in Atiks' case, became the dining room. A zippered flap offered you quick access to the cargo box under the mattress.
The tent was made of high-quality Tencate fabric and came with a separate storm cover, so GentleTent advertised it as water-, storm-, and wind-proof. You can tell from the most recent experience that it is, indeed, wind- and water-proof. The manufacturer also promised it was UV-resistant.
The B Turtle was imagined as a solution for bikepackers and, best of all, an upgrade over anything they had been offered until then. It was a shelter off the ground, with a comfortable double bed inside and a space that would serve as dining space and changing room, also protected from the elements.
Photo: GentleTent It was, because of all these, a solution that would make bikepacking comfortable for longer stretches, without feeling like you've been to hell and back. The Atiks' outing shows that, indeed, it was quite a nice solution for longer stays in nature, in pairs, on e-bikes.
As already noted, what ended the B Turtle dream was high pricing. When we first checked it out in 2022, one unit was selling for €3,499 (approximately $3,900 at the current exchange rate), which, you will agree, is a whole lot of money for a tent with two bike wheels.
Via // Atik Family on YouTube
